title: Say each thing once
statement: Say each thing once and only to teach: no line restating the printed question or anything already said or shown, explaining the obvious, or competing with the learner's action.
example: An automated check warns when a guide line shares 60% or more of its content words with the question beside it.
detail: Review comments on a grade 3 reading course cut lines that repeated what the guide had just said or a label the screen already showed, and a review call removed prompts such as 'now tap the correct answer', which generated content kept producing, as inflating cognitive load and teaching nothing (`grade3-reading/course-renderer/docs/rules/content-and-copy.md`, lines 127-157). An attention audit of the course's screens then made the question print its ask once, with everything else framing it or adding to it, and a lint warns at 60% content-word overlap between a guide line and the question beside it. A QA invariant also bars printing a label, such as a blank's number, that the interface already shows.
against: Read-along in the same course pairs every spoken line with print: "Every spoken line has a printed home on the page, sentence for sentence." (`grade3-reading/course-renderer/docs/rules/audio-and-voiceover.md`, lines 93-94), so the ban holds against a second line that repeats a point, not against printing what the guide says. A repeat can be deliberate: the Grade 9 design specification pins the lesson's question to the top of every screen (`othello-archive/sources/Year 9 ELA- Lesson Design Specification for Devfactory.txt`, line 215).
